title.value: Vendor-neutral sequences and fully transparent workflows improve inter-vendor reproducibility of quantitative MRI
title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the beginning of the paper.
title.quote: Vendor-neutral sequences and fully transparent workflows improve inter-vendor reproducibility of quantitative MRI

analysis.description: The paper discusses the development and deployment of a vendor-neutral MRI workflow designed to improve the consistency of quantitative MRI measures (T1, MTR, MTsat) across different scanner vendors. The workflow utilizes a vendor-neutral 3D SPGR sequence and the RTHawk platform to minimize differences in MRI sequences and processing, achieving reduced inter-vendor variability and enhancing the reliability of multicenter clinical trials.

type.justification: The study is empirical as it involves the development, implementation, and testing of the vendor-neutral MRI sequence across different scanners and participants.
type.quote: We developed an end-to-end workflow that starts with a vendor-neutral acquisition and tested the hypothesis that vendor-neutral sequences decrease inter-vendor variability.

name.justification: The research focuses on improving MRI techniques, making it pertinent to the field of medical imaging.

name.justification: The paper extensively discusses the development and application of MRI sequences.
name.quote: We developed and deployed a vendor-neutral 3D spoiled gradient-echo (SPGR) sequence on three clinical scanners.

name.justification: The research aims to enhance the reliability of multicenter clinical trials through improved standardization of MRI techniques.
name.quote: The significant reduction of inter-vendor variability using vendor-neutral sequences has important implications for qMRI research and for the reliability of multicenter clinical trials.
